revision_note: Revised before any commit, following clarification of the estimand (W_m varies over (i,r); h_m is one fixed function per m; theta_m is a scalar; h_0(X_i) = pbar_i a.s.; sum_m theta_m + theta_res = E_i[V_i]). No estimate had been produced under the earlier draft, and the earlier draft was never committed, so this is a revision of v1 rather than a v2. Any change AFTER this file is committed must bump spec_id instead.
purpose: Pre-specified estimation and inference plan for the cross-fitted stage-attribution parameters theta_m of Appendix C (orthogonal score, exact empirical telescoping). Frozen BEFORE any theta estimate is evaluated against replication outcomes Y.

estimand.population: Two-stage law. Draw a study from the study population, which fixes its context X_i; then draw a run as a fresh realization of the model randomness U, which generates the stage outputs and the score given that context. One pooled observation is one (study, run) pair.
estimand.score_output: P = q_6, the model's own Q_HAT on a single run
estimand.W_m: A random vector whose realization at observation (i, r) is (X_i, p_{i,1:m}^{(r)}). It varies over BOTH studies and runs.
estimand.h_m: h_m(w) = E[P | W_m = w] under the two-stage law: one fixed measurable function per stage, indexed by neither i nor r. Under cross-fitting, one fitted function per fold, h_hat_m^{(-k)}.
estimand.key_identity: X_i sits inside every W_m, so conditioning on W_m recovers the per-study Doob mean of Proposition 4.1: h_m(W_m) = h_{i,m}^{(r)} almost surely, and in particular h_0(X_i) = pbar_i.
estimand.theta_m: A SCALAR, one number per stage: theta_m = E_i{ E_U[D_{i,m}^2] }, the study-averaged stage-m contribution. Not indexed by anything but m.
estimand.theta_res: E_i{ E_U[(P - h_{s-1})^2] }, the study-averaged irreducible residual
estimand.adding_up: sum_{m<s} theta_m + theta_res = E_i[V_i], the study-averaged run-to-run variance of the score
estimand.pooling_role: Pooling across (i, r) is purely an estimation device. It does not change the estimand.
estimand.telescoping_identity: sum_m phi_m + phi_res == (P - h_0)^2 per observation, for ANY fitted nuisances (Proposition C.1). Asserted to 1e-10 on every run.

chain.note: theta_1..theta_4 are the four upstream stage attributions; the fifth increment of the existing chain code (D5 = q_6 - h_4) IS theta_res, not a stage. Unit 2 (Credibility) is unscored; unit 7 (Verdict) is a deterministic function of q_6 and contributes a zero increment by construction.

nuisance_conditioning.X_i_is: the study's full context (the paper text and everything else the generating model sees), which is study-identifying. It is NOT a low-dimensional covariate vector.
nuisance_conditioning.consequence: Because X_i identifies the study, h_m is a WITHIN-STUDY conditional expectation. The estimation resource for the study-level location is that study's own R = 100 runs; the estimation resource for anything shared across studies is the n studies.
nuisance_conditioning.h_0_estimator: h_hat_0,i = study i's mean of q_6 over the runs OUTSIDE the current run-fold. This is the saturated nonparametric fit of the fixed function h_0 at the observed X values: on a study-identifying X, the only functions of X are 'a number per study', and the study's own run mean is that number.
nuisance_conditioning.h_m_estimator: h_hat_m^{(-k)}(X_i, prefix) = h_hat_0,i + g_hat_m^{(-k)}(prefix centered within study). g_hat_m is a POOLED map from the within-study-centered prefix to the within-study score deviation, fit off-fold across studies. g_hat_m is one function per fold, indexed by neither i nor r, as the estimand requires.
nuisance_conditioning.additivity_assumption: The primary spec assumes the prefix-to-score map is additive and common across studies, with all study context entering through h_hat_0,i. Neyman orthogonality makes the error from this approximation enter only quadratically. Sensitivity arm S6 relaxes it with covariate-by-prefix interactions.

rejected_option_coarse_X.what: Estimating h_0 by a cross-fitted pooled regression of the score on a low-dimensional covariate vector (log original N, |r|, indicator p < .001, plus missingness indicators) instead of the study's own runs. This was the earlier draft of this spec.
rejected_option_coarse_X.why_rejected: The identity h_0(X_i) = pbar_i requires X_i to pin down the study. A coarse X_i does not, and the shortfall does not vanish: it is added to the total, so the thetas would sum to E_i[V_i] PLUS the between-study residual E_i[(pbar_i - h_0_coarse)^2] rather than to E_i[V_i] alone. Measured on the actual runs (temp 0.7, GroupKFold over clusters), the coarse regression has NEGATIVE cross-fitted R-squared in all three corpora, i.e. it predicts a study's mean score worse than the grand mean does.
rejected_option_coarse_X.richest_available_X_also_fails: Substituting the embedding-LR out-of-fold probability (the richest study-level text summary in this repo, and itself outcome-trained) gives cross-fitted R-squared of -0.009 on RPP, leaving leakage at 3.6x the within-study target. No study-generalizing X_i available here can recover pbar_i.
rejected_option_coarse_X.status: Retained as diagnostic arm S7, reported as a demonstration of why h_0 is estimated within-study, never as a headline estimate.

crossfitting.two_layers: Both are required, and they remove different biases.

study_folds.splitter: GroupKFold over cluster_key (all runs and all claims of a cluster stay together)
study_folds.removes: the pooled map g_hat_m having seen the study it is scoring

run_folds.removes: h_hat_0,i containing the very run being scored, which would bias theta_res down by roughly V_i / R

crossfitting.finite_R_correction: E[(P - h_hat_0,i)^2] = V_i * (1 + 1/R_train) with R_train the runs used per study fit, so the raw residual term is inflated by 1/R_train. The reported theta_res multiplies by R_train/(R_train + 1); the uncorrected value is reported alongside. At R_train = 80 the correction is about 1.25%.
crossfitting.prediction_clipping: [0, 1] (h_m is a conditional expectation of a [0,1]-valued output)

primary.form: g_m ~ within-study-centered prefix scores, entered linearly, no interactions
primary.rationale: Deliberately simple and pre-specified, as the appendix requires. Neyman orthogonality makes nuisance error enter phi_m only quadratically, and the effective sample size is 21-88 clusters.

robustness.folds: identical fold assignment to the primary

rate_condition.requirement: the DML second-order bias term sqrt(n) * ||h_hat - h||^2 must be negligible
rate_condition.for_h_0: ||h_hat_0 - h_0||^2 is approximately E_i[V_i] / R, so the bias term is sqrt(n) * E_i[V_i] / R. It is driven by R, not by n.
rate_condition.verdict: negligible in all three corpora at R = 100; the within-study estimator comfortably satisfies the condition, which a study-generalizing regression on coarse covariates would not.

nuisance_learner.no_truncation: Negative theta_hat_m are reported as estimated. No clipping at zero before inference.

RPP.known_structure: Two paper clusters carry two claims each. rpp.49/rpp.50 have genuinely distinct 100-run prediction vectors (two different effects). rpp.148/rpp.149 have byte-identical prediction vectors (one generation set surfaced under two ids). Both pairs are kept as two claims to preserve the n=90 convention used by predict_embed_lr.py / predict_rf_replicability.py; the within-paper dependence is absorbed by the paper-level cluster in both fold assignment and the variance estimator.
RPP.deviation_from_existing_code: uq_bound/common.py groups runs by 'Study Title (O)', which pools rpp.49 and rpp.50's two distinct effect run-sets into one 200-run claim. This spec keys claims by altmejd_id instead.

CB.known_structure: 158 effects nested in 23 papers; each effect has its own independent 100 runs. The cluster is the PAPER, not the effect: 23 is the effective sample size for inference.

SSRP.known_structure: One study per paper; claim and cluster coincide.

missing_data.CB_primary: Complete-chain effects only: an effect is in scope when q_1..q_6 are jointly non-null on at least one run, and only its complete runs enter the fit (the current dropna behaviour of common_cb.py, stated rather than incidental). Expected n is roughly 104 of 158 effects; the realized count is reported.
missing_data.CB_sensitivity: All 158 effects, q_1 imputed at its within-study mean with an availability dummy entering the prefix from stage 1 onward.
missing_data.RPP_SSRP: No chain-level missingness rule needed; realized run counts are reported.

inference.estimated_quantity: the five SCALARS theta_1..theta_4 and theta_res. Inference attaches to these and to nothing else.
inference.point_estimate: theta_hat_m = n^-1 sum_i R_i^-1 sum_r phi_{ir,m}, i over claims
inference.cluster_unit: cluster_key of the corpus (paper for RPP and CB, study for SSRP)

standard_error.method: cluster-robust: {n(n-1)}^-1/2 * {sum_i (phibar_{i,m} - theta_hat_m)^2}^1/2 over clusters, normal critical values -- applied identically to all three corpora, exactly as the appendix's Cross-fitting and inference paragraph states it. No small-G variant (jackknife, CR3, wild-cluster) is part of the request; none is used.
standard_error.reported_alongside: a study-cluster bootstrap interval (from the same multiplier-bootstrap draws as the simultaneous band below), per the appendix's own 'at n=90 we report study-cluster bootstrap intervals alongside' -- applied to all three corpora, not RPP only.

simultaneous_bands.statistic: sup_m |sum_i xi_i (phibar_{i,m} - theta_hat_m)| / se_hat_m over the 5 scalars jointly

per_claim_profiles.definition: theta_hat_{i,m} = the within-claim average of phi_{ir,m}, obtained by evaluating the fitted h_hat_m on claim i's own runs
per_claim_profiles.status: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. These are estimates, not exact per-claim decompositions, and carry no confidence intervals. Every figure and table showing them must be labeled descriptive.
per_claim_profiles.rationale: theta_m is a scalar estimand; the per-claim profile is a diagnostic view of the same fitted nuisances, not a second estimand with its own inference.

adding_up_check.what: sum_m theta_hat_m + theta_hat_res must reproduce the study-averaged run-to-run variance E_i[V_i], which is directly computable from the runs as the mean within-claim sample variance of q_6.
adding_up_check.tolerance: agreement to within the finite-R correction (about 1.25%) after that correction is applied; a larger gap means the nuisances are not respecting h_0 = pbar_i and the run fails loudly.
adding_up_check.note: This check is what distinguishes a correct within-study h_0 from the rejected coarse-X option, which would overshoot these targets by 241 to 399 percent.

coverage_simulation.source: the TODO's literal text: 'the n=90, R=100 coverage simulation' -- a single validation exercise, not a multi-arm design. No misspecification check, null-stage check, unequal-cluster check, or R-sweep is requested; none is run.
coverage_simulation.dgp: Two-stage, matching the clarified law: draw a study-level context that fixes pbar_i, then draw R runs given that context, with a correctly-specified additive linear prefix map (the estimator's own assumed functional form). The study-level location is deliberately NOT predictable from any observed covariate, matching the measured cross-fitted R-squared of about zero in all three corpora.
coverage_simulation.checks: whether the cluster-robust pointwise CI and the multiplier-bootstrap simultaneous band (the same two intervals reported on the real corpora) achieve their nominal 95% coverage at this n and R

per_corpus_table: theta_hat_m for the four stages and the residual
reporting.scope_guard: Section 4.1's per-claim plug-in v_hat_i in freedman_bound.py and validation_plot*.py is NOT modified by this work. The cross-fitted theta layer is added alongside, and the gap between the summed cross-fitted stage attributions and the mean plug-in v_hat_i is reported as a diagnostic of the plug-in's in-sample optimism.

implementation.adapters: corpus-specific claim key, cluster key and prediction path supplied by common.py, common_cb.py, common_ssrp.py; no estimator logic duplicated per corpus
implementation.parity_check: each corpus's phi matrix is hashed and the hash recorded in the run log, so a later refactor of the adapters can be shown to be inert
assertions: Proposition C.1 holds per observation to 1e-10 on all three corpora
no cluster appears in both the fit and evaluation side of any study fold
no run appears in both the fit and evaluation side of its run fold
g_hat_m is a single fitted object per fold, never indexed by claim
the adding-up check matches E_i[V_i] within tolerance
realized R_i and claim counts match this spec's corpora block, or the run fails loudly

sensitivity_arms.S5: temperature 0.2 prediction files in place of 0.7
sensitivity_arms.S6: study-covariate-by-prefix interactions in g_m, relaxing additivity
sensitivity_arms.S7: the rejected coarse-X h_0, reported only as the diagnostic that motivates the within-study estimator
